findings.title: Hacking Two Automakers: ForgeRock Path Confusion, RCE, and Remote Vehicle Access
findings.summary_md: Shubham Shah and Sam Curry describe a vulnerability chain giving remote code execution on the production ForgeRock servers handling customer logins for two unnamed automakers, discovered in early 2026 and reported the same day it was validated. Both automakers remediated within about two hours and rotated the affected credentials, and the affected systems served customers in multiple regions. The chain allowed creating a valid session for any customer account and, where a connected vehicle was present, remote access including location, door lock and unlock, and remote engine start and stop; only US accounts and vehicles were tested end to end.

findings.title: unlocking any car from X brand in most of the world
findings.summary_md: Shubham Shah details an Australia-focused chain against the same two automakers' connected-car platforms: a publicly exposed admin tool with hardcoded API keys, leaked OpenIDM admin credentials in a vendor JavaScript bundle, a WAF bypass via path traversal (`/static%2f..%2fopenidm/`), and an MFA bypass via the ROPC flow, enabling remote unlock and engine start from a license plate. Combined with Sam Curry's US and Canada work, the research covered vehicles in Australia, the United States, and Canada. The automakers were not named and fixed the issues shortly after disclosure.
